title: Check yourself: dynamic creation and invocation

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: At startup a metrics library calls Class.forName(name) on every class in its sinks package, logging and skipping any Throwable. One of them, StatsdSink, declares `static final String HOST = requireEnv("STATSD_HOST")`, which throws when the variable is unset, as it is on the staging host. Later on staging a request handler runs `new StatsdSink()`. What do the startup scan and the request see?

options.text: The scan loads StatsdSink without error, since forName(name) only loads; the request's new throws ExceptionInInitializerError
options.says: the one-argument forName initialises the class, so requireEnv runs and fails during the scan

options.text: The scan loads StatsdSink without error, since forName(name) only loads; the request's new throws NoClassDefFoundError
options.says: the one-argument forName initialises the class, so the scan already sees the failure

options.text: The scan logs an ExceptionInInitializerError, since forName(name) initialises; the request's new throws NoClassDefFoundError
options.says: forName(name) runs the static initialiser, which fails; a failed initialiser is not retried, and every later use throws NoClassDefFoundError: Could not initialize class

options.text: The scan logs an ExceptionInInitializerError, since forName(name) initialises; the request's new throws ExceptionInInitializerError
options.says: the JVM does not run a failed initialiser again; later uses get NoClassDefFoundError

origin.section: Class.forName(name) Runs the Static Initialiser; the Three-Argument Form Waits for First Use

questions.stem: A job runner's runAll() declares no exceptions. For each job class it runs `try { Object job = jobClass.newInstance(); ... } catch (ReflectiveOperationException e) { log.warn(...); continue; }`. ArchiveJob's constructor is declared `throws SQLException`, and today it throws one because the database is in maintenance. What happens when runAll() reaches ArchiveJob?

options.text: The catch logs a warning and the loop goes on, since newInstance() reports the SQLException wrapped in an InvocationTargetException
options.says: Class.newInstance() does not wrap; only Constructor.newInstance() wraps in InvocationTargetException

options.text: The catch logs a warning and the loop goes on, since newInstance() reports a constructor that throws as an InstantiationException
options.says: Class.newInstance() rethrows the constructor's own exception, checked or not

options.text: The SQLException passes the catch and leaves runAll(), since newInstance() rethrows the constructor's exception as it is
options.says: Class.newInstance() propagates the constructor's checked exception undeclared, so a catch of ReflectiveOperationException doesn't see it

options.text: The SQLException can't occur at run time, since javac refuses a runAll() that reaches a constructor throwing it undeclared
options.says: javac sees only newInstance()'s declared InstantiationException and IllegalAccessException; it compiles

origin.section: Class.newInstance Lets the Constructor's Checked Exception Escape Undeclared

questions.stem: A host looks up `MethodHandle h = lookup.findVirtual(Thumbnailer.class, "resize", methodType(byte[].class, byte[].class, int.class))`. Elsewhere it calls `Object out = h.invokeExact(thumbnailer, image, 320);`, where thumbnailer is declared as Thumbnailer and image as byte[]. What happens?

options.text: javac rejects the line, since the result is assigned to Object while the handle's type returns byte[]
options.says: invokeExact is signature-polymorphic: javac records the call site's type and checks nothing against the handle

options.text: javac rejects the line, since a call to invokeExact needs a cast to the handle's return type
options.says: javac accepts any call site type for invokeExact; a missing cast only makes the call site's return type Object

options.text: It compiles and throws WrongMethodTypeException, since the call site's type returns Object rather than byte[]
options.says: invokeExact requires the call site's type to equal the handle's, and (Thumbnailer,byte[],int)Object is not (Thumbnailer,byte[],int)byte[]

options.text: It compiles and returns the resized image, since a byte[] result can be assigned to Object without a conversion
options.says: invokeExact allows no upcasting of the result; only invoke() adapts the type

origin.section: A Method Handle Has a Type, and invokeExact Holds the Call Site to It

questions.stem: At startup a service runs `Class<? extends Notifier> type = (Class<? extends Notifier>) Class.forName(configured, false, loader);` and keeps type. The config names com.example.mail.SmtpSettings, a class that exists and has a public no-argument constructor but doesn't implement Notifier. Where does the ClassCastException come from?

options.text: At startup, from the cast, since casting the Class object compares SmtpSettings with Notifier
options.says: the cast to a parameterised Class type is unchecked and erased; nothing is compared at startup

options.text: At startup, from forName, since forName checks the loaded class against the bound of the variable
options.says: forName knows only the name and the loader; the class exists, so it loads

options.text: Later, from the line that takes the first new instance as a Notifier, since only that line checks the object
options.says: the unchecked cast passes, and the line that takes the first instance as a Notifier fails; asSubclass would have failed at startup

options.text: Later, from the first Notifier method called on the instance, since only that call checks the method
options.says: the check where the instance is taken as a Notifier fails before any Notifier method can be called

origin.section: A Class Named in Configuration Fails at First Use, Unless Startup Resolves It

concepts: A static initialiser that throws gives ExceptionInInitializerError once; every later use of the class throws NoClassDefFoundError and the initialiser is not run again.
invokeExact compiles with any call-site types and throws WrongMethodTypeException at run time unless they equal the handle's type; invoke and asType adapt.
